mia-segal.notes: Mia Segal (1930-2025) was born in Jerusalem, a fifth-generation Jerusalemite. She was the first person Moshe Feldenkrais authorized as a practitioner. In 1957, Feldenkrais selected Mia as his only associate, and in 1958 he authorized her to practice with clients on her own. She was trained individually before his first group training (Tel Aviv 1969-1971) and remained his first assistant and collaborator for approximately two decades. Feldenkrais said of her: 'With you, I have reached summits that alone, I could not reach.' Together they were pioneers in the Human Potential Movement, collaborating with leaders from complementary disciplines. They explored traditional healing disciplines in Japan, where Mia received a black belt in judo from the Kodokan in Tokyo (1970). She taught at the Esalen Institute in Big Sur. During the SF Professional Training (1975-1978), she co-taught evening ATM classes with Gaby Yaron to audiences of over 100. Feldenkrais authorized Mia as a Trainer in the 1960s. In 1987, she and her daughter Leora Gaster co-founded the Mind Body Studies (MBS) Academy to carry forward the full scope of their work with Feldenkrais. The academy has trained hundreds of practitioners worldwide. She eventually worked independently from the international Feldenkrais guild organizations. She continued teaching advanced mentoring courses and private sessions online into her final years. Mia died peacefully on February 15, 2025, in California, at the age of 94.

yochanan-rywerant.notes: Yochanan Rywerant (born November 7, 1922, Czernowitz, Bukovina; died May 20, 2010, Tel Aviv, aged 87) was one of the most significant figures in the Feldenkrais Method. Born into a Jewish family in multilingual Czernowitz, he survived the Holocaust after being deported to Transnistria with his mother Shulamit Wurmbrand in 1941, enduring forced labor at Jagendorf's Foundry in Mogilev. After the war, he emigrated to Israel, studied mathematics and physics at The Hebrew University of Jerusalem, and worked as a mathematics teacher. In 1952, he began attending Feldenkrais's open ATM classes — one of the very earliest students, predating any formal training by nearly two decades. In 1969, Feldenkrais invited him among 13 individuals to form the first Tel Aviv professional training (1969-1971). Beginning in 1970, he worked alongside Feldenkrais in the same room at the Tel Aviv Institute for 15 years. His 1983 book 'The Feldenkrais Method: Teaching by Handling' — with a foreword by Feldenkrais himself — became the authorized FI training manual and remains in print through multiple editions. After Feldenkrais's death in 1984, Rywerant began conducting independent teacher trainings in 1986, starting in Stockholm with three successive basic trainings and a pioneering Trainers Training (1994-1996). His 18-week condensed basic training model, teaching ATM and FI in parallel from the start, was distinctive. In 2000 he published 'Acquiring the Feldenkrais Profession'; in 2008, 'Corollary Discharge, The Forgotten Link' synthesized five decades of practice into a neuroscientific framework. Known for rigorous scientific temperament and insistence on theoretical clarity, he believed the Method is reproducible and teachable rather than dependent on individual charisma. Declined to use trademarks on Feldenkrais-related terms on principle. His approach continues under the banner of 'Classical Feldenkrais' by his students. Devoted 58 years (1952-2010) to learning, teaching, and writing about the Method.

chava-shelhav.notes: Dr. Chava Shelhav (January 31, 1940 – July 22, 2025) was born in Israel. She was a member of the original 13 students trained by Feldenkrais in Tel Aviv (1969-1971), and served as his personal assistant in training programs worldwide including Amherst. MA from Boston University (1989 thesis on brain-damaged children), PhD from University of Heidelberg (1998 dissertation 'Movement as a Model of Learning'). Co-founded the Feldenkraiszentrum Chava Shelhav in Neuss, Germany in 1991 with Karen Schmidt-Paas, serving as Educational Director for over 30 years; over 1,500 Feldenkrais practitioners graduated. Served as Educational Director for approximately 30 four-year training programs in Israel, Germany, the US, and the UK. Collaborated with Professor Esther Thelen on infant motor development research. From decades of clinical work with infants she developed the Child'Space Method (Child'Space – Chava Shelhav Method), a developmental coaching approach applying Feldenkrais principles to babies and caregivers. Since 2002, trained practitioners in Child'Space across Israel, USA, Japan, Netherlands, Russia, Austria, and Argentina, certifying approximately 150 practitioners. Died July 22, 2025 after a serious illness.

gaby-yaron.notes: Gabriella Segal Yaron (1923, Romania — June 3, 1995, Boston, MA). Graduated from the Music Academy of Bucharest in piano studies. Emigrated to Palestine in 1941 and settled in Tel Aviv. In the late 1950s, health problems led her to FI lessons with Feldenkrais, and she became a regular at his Alexander Yanai classes. Studied anatomy at Rothschild Hospital. After the Tel Aviv training, Moshe asked Gaby to meet weekly to develop new ideas and exchange FI lessons. She developed a full practice in Tel Aviv with up to 18 weekly ATM classes. Invited as Assistant in the SF and Amherst trainings. During the SF years, she and Mia Segal co-taught evening ATM classes for 100+ people. Her success working with children led to invitations to present to development and rehabilitation professionals. She taught in training programs across Australia, Canada, USA, France, Italy, Sweden, Switzerland, Austria, Germany, and England. Directed training programs in Sweden, Austria, and the USA. In 1993 began Master Classes in Austria and Germany. In 1992, her FI lessons were videotaped during the Michigan training. Developed 'Integrating the Chest' lesson series during recovery from a severe car accident. After Feldenkrais's death, widely regarded as the greatest single influence on many senior Feldenkrais teachers and a master exponent of FI. The Feldenkrais Journal #10 was dedicated 'to the memory of Gabriella Segal Yaron who touched so many with her knowledge, her clarity and her joy.'

myriam-pfeffer.notes: Myriam Pfeffer (1928–2014) was one of the original 13 students trained by Feldenkrais in Tel Aviv (1969-1971). A former yoga teacher, she became Feldenkrais's close collaborator and assistant, working alongside him until the end of his active teaching life. In May 1978, she recorded on a handheld tape machine the eight ATM lessons Feldenkrais taught in French to Peter Brook's actors at the Théâtre des Bouffes du Nord in Paris — recordings unpublished until 2017 when edited by her daughter Sabine Pfeffer and François Combeau and released through the IFF. Credited with introducing the Feldenkrais Method to French-speaking Europe and Italy. After Feldenkrais's death in 1984, participated in founding meetings for both the IFF and EUROTAB. From 1985 onward organized and directed 15 professional training programs in France, many co-taught with daughter Sabine at the Accord Mobile center in Paris (founded 1988). Also taught in training programs across Europe, Israel, and the US. Contributed educational materials to the Centre National de la Danse. Died April 5, 2014.

alon-talmi.notes: Alon Talmi (October 7, 1914 – 2001) was born in Tel Aviv as Alon Feldman, son of journalist and activist Yehoshua Radler-Feldman Ha-Talmi (1880-1957), known as Rabbi Binyamin, a co-founder of Brit Shalom, the binationalist movement advocating coexistence between Arabs and Jews. In his youth politically active: participated in Chugim Marksistim (Marxist Circles of Left Poale Zion) in 1934. Distinguished scientist: in 1951 appointed scientific attache for Israel, participating in the December 1951 UNESCO conference in Paris for establishing a European center for nuclear research (precursor to CERN) as 'accredited observer and scientific consultant to Israel.' From 1960-1968 Associate Professor of Chemistry at Bar-Ilan University; from 1961 Professor of Chemistry and eventually Dean at Tel Aviv University. Met Moshe Feldenkrais in Paris in 1949; they became very close friends. Feldenkrais inscribed a book to him: 'For my friend Alon Talmi, whose conversations have helped me clarify my thoughts far more than I am willing to admit.' Instrumental in encouraging Feldenkrais to return to Israel. Enrolled in the inaugural 1969-1971 Tel Aviv training as one of the 'Group 13.' Worked closely with Eli Wadler during the training. After completing the program, left his university position entirely to devote himself to bodywork. Developed a set of twenty structured Functional Integration lessons, each built around a central functional theme examined from different positions. These 'touch lessons' (Berührungslektionen) emphasized both scientific precision and the importance of intuition. Published articles in Somatics magazine (1980-1983) and the German Zeitschrift für Körperpsychotherapie. In 1989, created video documentation of all twenty lessons with Nurit Sommer. Conducted only three European training programs — in Birach (Germany), Austria, and Italy. His authorized lineage includes Yehudit Silver ('Under the Oak,' named because 'alon' means 'oak' in Hebrew), Dr. Nurit Sommer (co-founded SIB/ISIB), and Martin Gruber (Talmi-Methode for performing arts). The book 'Lächelnde Elefanten' (Smiling Elephants) documents his approach. Died in Tel Aviv in 2001.

eli-wadler.notes: Eli Wadler (~1945–2023) was one of the original 13 students trained by Feldenkrais in Tel Aviv (1969-1971/72). At 24, he was the youngest of the group. Background in drug addiction treatment. After training, worked 12 years as Feldenkrais's personal assistant. In 1984, after Feldenkrais's death, became his practice successor, taking over the private practice and the Feldenkrais Institute in Tel Aviv. Established the Feldenkrais Method at the Zinman College of Physical Education and Sport Sciences at the Wingate Institute (Israel's leading sports college), making it an independent academic field of study. Directed accredited German-language training programs in Switzerland and Germany, including advanced continuing education at ZIST. Appeared in the 2007 Haim Levy documentary reuniting seven surviving original students. In August 2021, was one of only two surviving original students (with Chava Shelhav) to teach at the 'Fifty Years in Motion' Israeli Feldenkrais Festival; taught a German-language ATM lesson and gave a premiere interview on the evolution of the Method. The German-language book 'Feldenkrais Eli Wadler' (2003/2004) by Helmut Wehren consists of transcribed conversations about his life and path with Feldenkrais. Died May 2023.

shlomo-bracha.notes: Dr. Shlomo Bracha was a psychiatrist and neuroscientist who was one of the original 13 students trained by Feldenkrais in Tel Aviv (1969-1971). According to the Yochanan Rywerant memorial website, his contributions to the Method were 'invaluable,' particularly in explaining the brain, the central nervous system, and the shift between the unconscious and awareness. He helped establish the theoretical framework of the Method. The same source notes he 'is slightly forgotten.' No birth or death dates found. No publications, personal website, podcast appearances, or practitioner directory listings discovered. Was not among the seven surviving original students who reunited in the 2007 Haim Levy documentary. The Somatics articles on 'Functional Integration in Psychiatric Treatment' (1981) are by Alon Talmi, not Bracha, despite the psychiatric subject matter. Extremely limited online presence — mentioned only in passing on pages about the original 13 as a group. Do not confuse with H. Stefan Bracha (VA psychiatrist in Honolulu) — a different person.

batya-fabian.notes: Batya Fabian (also spelled Batia Fabian) was one of the original 13 students trained by Feldenkrais in Tel Aviv (1969-1971). Consistently described as a dancer who 'learned how to dance under Isadora Duncan,' making her one of the few members with a performing arts background. During the training, she paired with Gaby Yaron as practice partners, meeting every Saturday, and they studied anatomy together at Rothschild Hospital in Haifa. Given that Isadora Duncan died in 1927, Batya likely studied at one of the Duncan schools rather than with Duncan herself, placing her birth likely no later than the early 1920s. Beyond her inclusion in the roster and the Duncan dance note, virtually no biographical details survive online: no birth date, no death date, no publications, no recordings, no websites, and no known students. One of the smallest digital footprints of any member of the original 13. Unclear whether she continued to practice the Feldenkrais Method professionally after the training.

dvora-hasdai.notes: Dvora Hasdai was one of the original 13 students in Feldenkrais's first professional training (Tel Aviv, 1969-1971). A 2000 JWeekly article described her as one of Feldenkrais's 'star pupils' and noted she was still actively teaching in her 80s, placing her birth around 1920 or earlier. In 2007, filmmaker Haim Levy documented a reunion of seven surviving original students; those filmed included Hasdai along with Eli Wadler, Shlomo Efrat, Yochanan Rywerant, Chava Shelhav, and Bruria Milo (who died during filming). Unlike several cohort members who founded sub-methods or published extensively, Hasdai appears to have practiced and taught quietly in Israel without seeking international visibility. No personal website, publications, podcast appearances, or named notable students found. Online presence is extremely limited.

david-zemach-bersin.notes: David Zemach-Bersin is one of the foremost living authorities on the Feldenkrais Method and among the most important figures in its dissemination in the English-speaking world. He first met Dr. Moshe Feldenkrais in 1973 and studied with him continuously from 1973 to Feldenkrais's death in 1984, across the United States, England, and Israel. He is a graduate of Feldenkrais's first American professional training program in San Francisco (1975-1977), making him one of only approximately 80 people worldwide to have completed their entire training directly under Feldenkrais. In addition to his studies with Feldenkrais, he trained extensively with Gaby Yaron and Yochanon Rywerant, both graduates of Feldenkrais's original 1967 training in Tel Aviv. David holds an honors degree from the University of California, Berkeley, with extensive postgraduate work in physiological psychology. He has maintained a continuous private Feldenkrais practice since 1977. He served as President of the Feldenkrais Guild of North America (FGNA). He is the co-founder of three major Feldenkrais organizations: Feldenkrais Resources (co-founded in 1984 with Elizabeth Beringer), the primary publisher and distributor of Dr. Feldenkrais's English-language materials; the Feldenkrais Institute of New York; and the Feldenkrais Foundation, a nonprofit dedicated to research and bringing the Method to underserved populations. He has directed professional Feldenkrais training programs in New York City and Washington/Baltimore. He co-authored 'Relaxercise' (HarperOne, 1990) with his wife Kaethe Zemach-Bersin (children's book illustrator, daughter of Harve and Margot Zemach) and colleague Mark Reese. He wrote the foreword to 'Embodied Wisdom: The Collected Papers of Moshe Feldenkrais' (North Atlantic Books, edited by Elizabeth Beringer). Since approximately 2019-2020, he has directed Feldenkrais Access (feldenkraisaccess.com), an online platform offering over 60 on-demand Feldenkrais programs. He also teaches periodic in-person workshops, including at the Omega Institute in Rhinebeck, New York. David and his wife Kaethe have three grown children and live in Bucks County, Pennsylvania.

mark-reese.notes: Mark Lawrence Reese (March 15, 1951 – June 23, 2006, San Rafael, CA) was one of the world's foremost authorities on the Feldenkrais Method. Led 30+ professional training programs across San Diego, LA, SF, Seattle, Detroit, NYC, Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane, Rome, Milan, Munich, and Toronto, training 1,000+ practitioners. In 1982 co-founded FSCMI with Donna Ray-Reese. His intellectual work was influenced by dynamic systems theory of Esther Thelen, Edward Reed, and Alan Fogel. Devoted last two decades to a definitive Feldenkrais biography; Volume One published posthumously (2015) by ReeseKress Somatic Press, completed by Carol Kress Reese and Clifford Skoog. dennis-leri.notes: Dennis Leri (July 31, 1945 – December 15, 2016) was one of the most influential Feldenkrais trainers in North America. Born in Marysville, CA, graduated Marysville High School 1963, BA from Chico State, MA from Sonoma State. Graduated SF training (1975-1977) and apprenticed with Feldenkrais at Tel Aviv Institute 1973-1984. Taught the Method for 40+ years, directed numerous training programs worldwide including the Somathematics training with Elizabeth Beringer (1988, Sonoma State), first Austrian training (1991), Vienna training with Carl Ginsburg (1995), Rocky Mountain 1 (2006-2009), and FRTI Berkeley 7 as Educational Director. Core faculty at FRTI with Beringer and Zemach-Bersin. Frequently co-taught with Carol Kress, producing the Mid-Summer's Dream Intensive series and 'Truly Advanced' extended trainings. 35+ years of martial arts (Aikido, Chen-style Tai Chi, Lan Shou Kung Fu, boxing, Chi Kung). Studied with hypnotherapist Milton Erickson. Practiced Buddhism with Jiyu Kennett Roshi, Tarthang Tulku Rinpoche, and Tenzin Wangyal Rinpoche (10+ years). Intellectual work drew on Francisco Varela, Humberto Maturana, Heinz von Foerster, Charles S. Peirce, and René Thom (from whom 'semiophysics' derives). Coined the concept of 'primitives' in Feldenkrais work and developed the 'Archimedean Lever' concept. Lived in San Rafael, CA with wife Maria.

elizabeth-beringer.notes: Elizabeth Beringer is one of the foremost Feldenkrais teachers and trainers, with more than 40 years of involvement in the practice and development of the Feldenkrais Method. She studied directly with Moshe Feldenkrais in both the U.S. and Israel from 1976 to 1983. She co-founded Feldenkrais Resources with David Zemach-Bersin in 1983 to develop and disseminate Feldenkrais-based educational programs. She founded and edited the Feldenkrais Journal for 18 years, the first journal dedicated to the method. Her main focus has been training new practitioners; she has directed four-year professional training programs in Switzerland, France, Italy, the UK, and various U.S. locations, having graduated her 13th training group. She is currently the educational director of ongoing training programs in the UK, Switzerland, and at the Feldenkrais Institute of San Diego. She is a partner at the Feldenkrais Resources Training Institute (FRTI) in Berkeley, California, alongside David Zemach-Bersin and Carol Kress. She has practiced aikido since 1977 and holds a 6th-degree black belt. Her current teaching integrates advances in the cognitive sciences into the Feldenkrais perspective. She lives in San Diego with her husband, Rafael Nunez, a professor of cognitive science at UC San Diego.

thomas-hanna.notes: Thomas Louis Hanna (November 21, 1928 – July 29, 1990) was a philosopher, author, and movement theorist who coined 'somatics' in 1976 and founded Hanna Somatic Education. BA in theology from Texas Christian University (1949), Bachelor of Divinity from U of Chicago (1954), PhD in philosophy and divinity from U of Chicago (1958). Held positions at Hollins College, guest lectured at UNC and Duke. At University of Florida studied neurology and developed his body-experience theory. In 1973 moved to SF and became director of the Humanistic Psychology Institute (later Saybrook Institute). That year attended Feldenkrais's month-long Berkeley workshop, witnessing Feldenkrais work with a man with cerebral palsy — an experience that changed his career. Through his HPI position, arranged for Feldenkrais to come to the US as Distinguished Visiting Professor. From 1975-1978, Feldenkrais trained 65 teachers at Lone Mountain College — the first American training. In 1975, co-founded the Novato Institute with wife Eleanor Criswell Hanna and launched Somatics magazine. Developed concepts of Sensory Motor Amnesia (SMA) and pandiculation. Codified three reflexive stress patterns: Green Light (Landau), Red Light (startle), and Trauma Reflex. In 1990 launched his first formal training with 38 students. Killed in a car accident July 29, 1990 near Novato at age 61. His 38 original students became the first generation of certified Hanna Somatic Educators.

carl-ginsburg.notes: Carl Ginsburg, Ph.D. (1936-2018) was a scientist, former professor of chemistry, and one of the most intellectually distinguished figures in the Feldenkrais community. He received his Ph.D. in Chemistry from Ohio University in 1964. He studied directly with Moshe Feldenkrais during the first North American training program in San Francisco (1975-1977) and was one of Feldenkrais's first American students. He taught in and later directed professional training groups for Feldenkrais practitioners for 30 years. He served as past president of the Feldenkrais Guild of North America. He was involved for many years with the Shake-A-Leg Program, working with individuals with spinal injuries. His book 'The Intelligence of Moving Bodies,' written with his wife Lucia Schuette-Ginsburg and published by AWAREing Press in Santa Fe, New Mexico, braids together science, first-person narrative, and insights into the Feldenkrais Method. He was known for his beautiful literary constructions and for bringing scientific rigor to the understanding of somatic practices. He wrote the foreword to the North Atlantic Books reissue of Feldenkrais's 'Body and Mature Behavior.' A memorial evening, 'An Evening of Remembering Carl Solomon Ginsburg,' was held on May 23, 2019 at The Feldenkrais Institute in New York.

jerry-karzen.notes: Jerry Karzen is a Senior Feldenkrais Trainer with over four decades of experience teaching and training the Feldenkrais Method. He was the first Executive Director of the Feldenkrais Foundation and has served as President of the Feldenkrais Guild of North America. Since 1980, he has been the Organizer/Educational Director for approximately 40 training programs in 9 countries, including Germany, China, Brazil, New Zealand, and Russia. He is highly regarded for his ability to interpret and explain Feldenkrais's Functional Integration lessons and is known for his clear, concise, open-ended, exploratory, and non-directive teaching style. His 'In Tune with Yourself' workshops for musicians, recorded in Vienna with participants including members of the Vienna Symphony Orchestra, have been particularly well received.

russell-delman.notes: Russell Delman's exploration of body/mind awareness and human potential began in 1969 as an undergraduate psychology student, when he also began practicing Zen meditation. He deepened his self-knowledge through workshops at the Esalen Institute (1971), living at the Gestalt Institute of Canada (1972), traveling in the jungles of South America (1973), yoga teacher training (1974), and studying Gestalt therapy with Dr. Robert Hall (1975-1978). His training and deep personal relationship with Moshe Feldenkrais began in 1975 during the first U.S. professional program in San Francisco, and he graduated in 1977. In 1984, he became one of the first people in the world authorized to lead Feldenkrais Professional Training Programs, and has since taught in over 50 such programs internationally. In 1993, he developed The Embodied Life, an integrated learning program combining Feldenkrais Method, Zen meditation (influenced by studying with Jakusho Kwong Roshi in the lineage of Shunryu Suzuki since 1972), and Focusing (deeply influenced by a close personal friendship with its creator, Eugene Gendlin, beginning around 2006). Along with his wife Linda Delman, also a Feldenkrais Trainer, he created the Feldenkrais-India Project, bringing the method to India for the first time through work at Mother Teresa's Missions in Calcutta, teaching the Sisters of Charity to work with brain-injured children. He lives in Sebastopol, in Sonoma County, California, and has been married approximately 50 years. He is a faculty member at the Esalen Institute and was a presenter at The Embodiment Conference. He later created The Embodied Life Mentorship Program (ELMP), a three-year immersion program.

paul-rubin.notes: Paul Rubin was born around 1949 (he was 24 years old in 1973). In 1973, he was at the Esalen Institute in Big Sur, California, running a school for troubled adolescents on a grant from the government of Canada's Department of Health and Welfare, when Moshe Feldenkrais and Ida Rolf came to dinner. That encounter changed his life. He enrolled in the first North American Feldenkrais Professional Training in San Francisco in 1975 and graduated in 1977, making him one of only approximately 80 people to have completed training entirely under Dr. Feldenkrais. In 1992, he and his wife Julie Casson Rubin founded the Institute for the Study of Somatic Education (ISSE), a 501(c)(3) nonprofit corporation based at 1158 Naples Street in San Francisco. As Executive Director and co-Educational Director of ISSE, Paul co-directed certification training programs for Feldenkrais teachers in Cincinnati, Chicago, San Francisco, Houston, Australia, Switzerland, Italy, and Taiwan, graduating over 900 Feldenkrais Teachers worldwide across 19 training programs. He has also been active in the education of musicians, dancers, and actors regarding skill acquisition and efficient self-use, contributing articles to the Suzuki Association of the Americas connecting the Feldenkrais Method to music pedagogy. After 45+ years of practice, he now primarily serves as Educational Director and Guest Faculty in teacher training programs and provides post-graduate education. ISSE announced it would no longer provide the four-year training programs, with current programs ending in stages by 2026, though Paul and Julie may continue to teach as guest faculty. He and Julie are parents of four young adults.

julie-casson-rubin.notes: Julie Casson Rubin holds a degree in Dance and Physical Education from San Francisco State University. She trained directly with Dr. Moshe Feldenkrais at his first North American training in San Francisco beginning in 1975 and graduated in 1977. From 1977 to 1988, she was on staff at the pioneering Behavioral Medicine Clinic at San Francisco General Hospital (UCSF), where she was instrumental in bringing the Feldenkrais Method into clinical use beginning in 1979. In 1988, she co-founded the Feldenkrais Center for Movement and Awareness (FCMA) in San Francisco with Deborah Bowes; the center operated for 32 years before closing in August 2020 due to the COVID-19 pandemic. In 1996, she was responsible for introducing the Feldenkrais Method to the Health Education Department at Kaiser Permanente. She and her husband Paul Rubin founded ISSE in 1992 and have co-directed 19 training programs in the United States, Taiwan, Australia, Switzerland, and Italy. Her professional presentations include diverse groups such as the American Physical Therapy Association, Workers' Compensation Nurses and Case Managers, UCSF Medical Students, Kaiser Dermatology Department, Catholic Social Services, Sonoma Valley Hospital, UC Davis Pain Management Conference, Buen Dia Family School, Pacific Association of Women Martial Artists, and St. Francis Hospital Women Physicians group. She has authored and recorded specialized Feldenkrais Awareness Through Movement programs addressing chronic pain and pelvic floor issues. She is currently working at Stanford Hospital with people who have complex and persistent medical conditions, in addition to maintaining her private practice. She and Paul are parents of four young adults.

jack-heggie.notes: Jack Heggie earned a degree in physics and worked as a digital computer design engineer, programmer, and field engineer for ten years before becoming a Feldenkrais Practitioner. He became interested in the Feldenkrais Method in the mid-1970s while Dr. Feldenkrais was still alive, attended several public workshops with him in the US, then traveled to Israel to work with him personally. Heggie became a Feldenkrais Assistant Trainer and was internationally recognized for integrating the Feldenkrais Method into sports performance, particularly running, skiing, and golf. He also developed a vision improvement program combining Awareness Through Movement with Dr. William Bates' techniques. Heggie maintained a private practice in Boulder, Colorado and Dallas, Texas, and conducted workshops on running, golf, skiing, and vision improvement. He moved to Boulder so that he could work less and write more. He translated Feldenkrais' 25 lessons from Eshkol-Wachman movement notation into English, a significant contribution to the preservation of Feldenkrais' original teaching material. In his last letter, he critiqued the commercialization and poor teaching standards within Feldenkrais training programs. He died in 2002, reportedly by suicide.

frank-wildman.notes: Dr. Frank Wildman is a former professional dancer who holds degrees in Physical Education, Biology, and Somatic Psychology. He studied with Dr. Moshe Feldenkrais for over a decade and became one of the most influential figures in institutionalizing and spreading the Feldenkrais Method worldwide. After Feldenkrais' death in 1984, Wildman directed the first accredited Practitioner Training Programs. As president of the Feldenkrais Guild of North America, he formulated the Standards of Practice that became the current international guidelines for the Feldenkrais Method. In 1985, he founded the Movement Studies Institute (also known as the Feldenkrais Movement Institute of Berkeley), which trained the largest number of Feldenkrais practitioners of any organization. He has directed over thirty professional training programs in the United States, Japan, Europe, and Australia, and introduced the work of Feldenkrais to organizations including the Australian Institute for Sport and the American Back Society. His private practice is based in Berkeley, California. Wildman developed The Intelligent Body method, a system of neuroplastic movement integrating modern neuroscience with physical motion, and the Change Your Age program for healthy aging. He has trained hundreds of physical therapists in seven countries and has been a HuffPost contributor.

anat-baniel.notes: Anat Baniel was born in Israel in 1949. BA in Psychology and Statistics from Hebrew University of Jerusalem, MA in Clinical Psychology from Tel Aviv University. Trained dancer. First encountered Feldenkrais at age five when he came to her parents' home. At age seven began studying with a ballet teacher who was a Feldenkrais student. Joined SF training 1975, graduated 1977. Invited to work at Feldenkrais Institute in Tel Aviv 1977-1981, became trainer 1981. Worked side by side with Feldenkrais seeing clients. When Feldenkrais fell ill in Zurich, he asked Baniel to help bring him home. They remained close until his death in 1984. Developed the Anat Baniel Method NeuroMovement, centered on the Nine Essentials. Neuroscientist Michael Merzenich (2016 Kavli Prize) endorsed her work. Built the ABM Center in San Rafael (Marin County) in 2006. Over 1,000 practitioners trained worldwide through ABMI. TEDxBerkeley talk 2011. Published peer-reviewed research in Frontiers in Integrative Neuroscience (2025). In 1999, a lawsuit challenged the Feldenkrais Guild's ownership of service marks, partly related to Baniel's training practices; settled out of court ~2000. She subsequently branded her work as a separate modality. Featured in Norman Doidge's The Brain's Way of Healing (2015). Endorsed by Michael Merzenich, Norman Doidge, Arianna Huffington, Jack Canfield.

steven-shafarman.notes: Steven Shafarman studied philosophy, psychology, and human development in college. A few months after graduating in 1976, he met Dr. Moshe Feldenkrais and enrolled in the first North American professional training program at Lone Mountain College in San Francisco. He studied with Feldenkrais from 1976 to 1984, becoming a certified Feldenkrais practitioner and assistant trainer. In 1981, when Feldenkrais last taught in the United States, he asked Shafarman to travel with him as his assistant and appointments secretary. As a Feldenkrais practitioner, Shafarman taught in Europe, Israel, Argentina, Australia, and across the United States, and also studied and taught yoga and other movement education approaches. His 1997 book Awareness Heals was the first book to present the full benefits of the Feldenkrais Method in accessible, clear language. He later enrolled in a doctoral program in human development, and his research into how young children learn to crawl, walk, and talk inspired him to create FlexAware, a fitness practice based on principles from child development and the Feldenkrais Method; the first FlexAware DVD was released in 2010. Shafarman's career has a notable second dimension: he has been a leading advocate for universal basic income since the mid-1980s, authoring six books on the topic and serving as program director of Basic Income Action in Washington, D.C., and as a life member of the Basic Income Earth Network (BIEN). He delivered a TEDxMidAtlantic talk on universal basic income in 2018.

stephen-rosenholtz.notes: Dr. Stephen Rosenholtz was a former classroom teacher who earned his master's degree in Education from Harvard University in 1971 and his doctorate in Education from Stanford University in 1981, where his research focused on the nature of ability formation and self-image. mara-della-pergola.notes: Mara Della Pergola is the first Italian Feldenkrais practitioner and one of the most experienced practitioners in Europe, with over 40 years of practice and teaching. She was the sole Italian student of Moshe Feldenkrais, training with him in the Amherst course (1980-1983). Her background is in the psychosocial field and theater. In 1983 she began teaching, leaving her work in the socio-health field. In 1987, together with Italian colleagues then attending the Paris school training, she co-founded the Italian Association of Feldenkrais Method Teachers (AIIMF), serving as president until 1992. In 1988 she founded the Istituto di Formazione Feldenkrais (IsFel) in Milan to disseminate the Method, organizing the first Italian training with approximately sixty participants and Ruthy Alon as pedagogical director. For many years she worked with the most experienced first-generation teachers including Gaby Yaron, Myriam Pfeffer, Ruthy Alon, Yochanan Rywerant, Chava Shelhav, Bruria Milo, and Mark Reese. She has taught in Europe, North and South America, Russia, and China, and is known for her clarity, creativity, and accessibility. She is the pedagogical director of IsFel and continues to direct ongoing training programs in Milan (currently Milano 11). Her 2017 book 'Lo sguardo in movimento' (Vision in Motion: Art, Transformation and the Feldenkrais Method), published by Astrolabio-Ubaldini, explores the intersection of art and the Feldenkrais Method and forms part of the curriculum in her training programs.

roger-russell.notes: Roger Russell (b. 1951, Denver, Colorado) is an American physical therapist, movement scientist, and Feldenkrais Trainer who has lived in Heidelberg, Germany for decades. linda-tellington-jones.notes: Linda Tellington-Jones (b. June 30, 1937, Edmonton, Alberta, Canada) is a Canadian-born animal trainer, healer, and author who created the Tellington TTouch Method. She became a riding instructor at age 13. In the 1960s, she and her first husband Wentworth Tellington founded the Pacific Coast Equestrian Research Center in Badger, California. In 1975, she enrolled in Feldenkrais's professional training at the Humanistic Psychology Institute in San Francisco, graduating in 1978. She applied Feldenkrais principles of non-habitual movement and neural pathway activation to animals, inventing the circular touches that became TTouch in 1983. The method has grown to 1,700+ certified practitioners in 37 countries. Inducted into the U.S. Massage Hall of Fame (2007); honorary doctorate from Wisdom University (2008). She has written 23+ books in 15-16 languages. Her biography is 'Strike a Long Trot' by Shannon Yewell Weil (2013). Lives in Hawaii with husband Roland Kleger. ellen-soloway.notes: Ellen Soloway is a Certified Feldenkrais Practitioner and Assistant Trainer, and the editor of the English-language Alexander Yanai Volumes — the foundational archival collection of nearly 600 Awareness Through Movement lessons that Moshe Feldenkrais taught weekly in Tel Aviv from the early 1950s to late 1970s. She had the distinction of studying with Dr. Feldenkrais across three settings: San Francisco (1975-1977), Amherst (1980-1983), and Israel, spanning 1975 to 1982. She maintains a private practice and offers Functional Integration lessons and mentoring in New Orleans, Atlanta, San Antonio, and Chicago, as well as online via Zoom. She offers guided 1:1 Awareness Through Movement classes, Feldenkrais Method workshops, and Practitioner Mentoring sessions. She has taught the 'Well-Trained Hands' advanced workshop for practitioners, focusing on developing refined hand and arm sensitivity for Functional Integration work. She offered a Feldenkrais Mastery Course with an Eye Specialty focus (May 2016). She was interviewed for the Feldenkrais Guild's SenseAbility Magazine. She presented at the Feldenkrais Guild's 'Chat with a Feldenkrais Trainer' series (June 2021). The Alexander Yanai volumes she edited were translated by Anat Baniel and Jeremy Krauss, with additional translators and proofreaders including Bonnie Humiston, Marcy Lindheimer, Nancy Schumacher, and Penny McCornack. No specific birth year, birth location, named students, or book-length authored publications (beyond her editorial work) were found in research. No evidence of being deceased.

beatriz-walterspiel.name: Beatriz Walterspiel
beatriz-walterspiel.relationship: Trained by Moshe Feldenkrais in America 1980-1983.
beatriz-walterspiel.notes: Internationally recognized Trainer since 1993. Led trainings in Argentina, Germany, Scandinavia, and Spain. Background in Middendorf respiratory therapy and Gindler movement work. Published 'Das Abenteuer der Bewegung: Die Feldenkrais Methode' (1989).

sabine-pfeffer.name: Sabine Pfeffer
sabine-pfeffer.relationship: Trained directly by Moshe Feldenkrais in Israel and the US; completed training at Amherst 1983. Daughter of Myriam Pfeffer (Tel Aviv 13).
sabine-pfeffer.notes: Founded Accord Mobile center in Paris (1988), training the first French practitioners. Led 15 training programs in France. Key figure in bringing the Method to France.

aliza-stewart.name: Aliza Stewart
aliza-stewart.relationship: Brought to Moshe Feldenkrais in 1980; completed Feldenkrais training 1987.
aliza-stewart.notes: Concert pianist who created Embodied Music, adapting Feldenkrais for musicians. Taught at Peabody Institute and Mannes College of Music. Educational Director of Boston Feldenkrais Training.

katrin-smithback.name: Katrin Smithback
katrin-smithback.relationship: Began studies with Moshe Feldenkrais in 1980.
katrin-smithback.notes: Editor of the Feldenkrais Journal. Faculty at College of Santa Fe for 17 years. Educational Director of trainings in Japan and Argentina. Continuous private practice in Santa Fe since 1981.

yvan-joly.name: Yvan Joly
yvan-joly.relationship: Certified as practitioner-teacher from Amherst training in 1983, Trainer since 1995.
yvan-joly.notes: M.A. in Psychology from Universite de Montreal. Co-founder and first president of Quebec Regrouping for Somatic Education. Founded Feldenkrais Institute of Somatic Education (1992). Trained practitioners in 15 countries across 4 continents. Pioneer in establishing the academic field of somatic education.

david-kaetz.name: David Kaetz
david-kaetz.relationship: Trained by Dr. Feldenkrais, graduated Amherst 1983.
david-kaetz.notes: Author of 'Making Connections: Roots and Resonance in the Life of Moshe Feldenkrais' (2007, 2nd ed. 2014) — the most significant intellectual/biographical study of Feldenkrais's Jewish and cultural roots. Developer of 'Listening with Your Whole Body' integrative hearing approach. Canadian musician and writer.

angel-di-benedetto.name: Angel Di Benedetto
angel-di-benedetto.relationship: Began studies with Dr. Feldenkrais in 1980 at Amherst.

jeremy-krauss.name: Jeremy Krauss
jeremy-krauss.relationship: Direct student of Dr. Moshe Feldenkrais.
jeremy-krauss.notes: Directed 28+ training programs in Europe, USA, Japan, and Israel. Developed the Jeremy Krauss Approach (JKA) for special needs children. Published 'Developing Potential in Children with Special Needs' (2023). Chosen by IFF to translate Feldenkrais archival material. Lives in Germany.

john-quinn.name: John Quinn
john-quinn.relationship: GCFP certified 1999. Second-generation practitioner. Presented at 2006 FGNA Conference at Omega, NY.
john-quinn.deceased: unknown (FGNA NY Region library named 'John Quinn Memorial Library', implying deceased)

john-quinn.notes: GCFP (1999), BFL(T) (Bones for Life Teacher), Sounder Sleep System teacher. Also a professional actor, playwright, and stage director — member of AEA, SAG, AFTRA. Retired QDE (Qualified Designated Examiner). Based in New York. The FGNA New York Region maintains a 'John Quinn Memorial Library' of Feldenkrais materials, suggesting he was a significant figure in the NY Feldenkrais community and is deceased. His personal website (panix.com/~johnquinn) is no longer online. Limited online footprint beyond the openATM Bell Hand recording and LinkedIn profile.
